AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
5:00 P.M. CLOSED SESSION

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Rebollo called meeting to order at 5:01 p.m.

RECONVENE TO OPEN SESSION City Council/Successor Agency reconvened to Open Session at 6:28 p.m.

ORAL CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT City Attorney Tapia reported on item #1 on Closed Session agenda and stated that staff made a presentation, feedback was provided and no reportable action was taken on this item.  

6:00 P.M. - CITY COUNCIL MEETING

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Rebollo called regular City Council meeting to order at 6:30 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE City Manager Cisneros led the Pledge of Allegiance.

INVOCATION Mayor Rebollo offered the invocation.

APPEARANCES AND PRESENTATIONS

1.. Presentation/Update from the Sheriff's Department Regarding Public Safety in the City of Commerce Sergeant Villarreal provided a 30-day update regarding public safety in the CIty of Commerce. COPS Team investigated crimes in Commerce, and the traffic sergeant conducted traffic enforcement. 

Discussion took place about enforcement of illegal fireworks and fines, and it was a consensus among the City Council that more information needs to be brought and discussed. 

Sergeant Villarreal noted that illegal fireworks are a misdemeanor, and deputies could increase patrol during this time to stop the discharge of illegal fireworks. 


PUBLIC COMMENT There were no individuals wishing to address the City Council on any items within their jurisdiction. 

Director of Administrative Services and City Clerk Shumway stated that public comments requests received for previous meetings/items on the previous agenda would be entered in the minutes for the record. These comments are the following:

Maria Valdez wrote about new transportation routes. Bus route change has made it difficult for her to participate in her cherished Sunday routine that included attending Sunday church services, Casino sponsored lunch, and time with friends. Ms. Valdez asked for the routes to be returned to how they were.

Nicolasa Sandoval expressed concern with all the recent changes in the Transportation department. Shortage of drivers, reduced staff to answer calls and answer questions, and the lack of bilingual staff. Ms. Sandoval expressed concern for her safety if drivers are being asked to work extra hours solely to continue with the current schedules since this causes fatigue, and asked if staff could look into her concerns to ensure there are no violations.

Gloria Nezagulacoyotl expressed discontent with the Transportation Director's lack of interest which has affected residents in various parts of the City. The changes to the City Bus Routes now require passengers to walk long distances just to board the bus; church routes and the Casino-sponsored Sunday lunch route have been removed. Calls, complaints, and suggestions are ignored by the department. 





CONSENT CALENDAR  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Ivan Altamirano Councilmember Soria asked to pull item #9 from the Consent Calendar.  

Item #9 - Councilmember Soria recused himself from participating on this item due to a potential conflict of interest. 

Mayor Rebollo moved, seconded by Vice Mayor Argumedo, to adopt a Resolution awarding a construction contract to Hardy & Harper, Inc. for the FY 2021-22 Pavement Rehabilitation Project and authorizing construction management and inspection services by Transtech Engineers, Inc., and geotechnical investigation and material testing services by Geo-Advantec, Inc. pursuant to their on-call Professional consulting services agreements.  The motion carried by the following vote: 

AYES: Councilmembers Altamirano, Mendoza, Vice Mayor Argumedo and Mayor Rebollo (4)
Recused: Councilmember Soria

According to Director Brooks, the preliminary surplus and revenue projections are subject to potential reductions due to various negative economic issues. 

Councilmember Mendoza asked that staff looks into the possibility of having a Commerce Police Department instead of contracting out services. Director Brooks stated that the City conducted the study and determined that contacting out would work best for the City. 

Councilmember Altamirano asked staff to look into opening all programs for residents.

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Councilmember Mendoza thanked Assemblywoman Garcia for working tirelessly to help with the clean-up of contamination of lead in the City of Commerce from Exide. 

Vice Mayor Argumedo spoke on item #13 on the agenda and thanked staff, volunteers, and residents for their hard work installing these speed humps. 

Mayor Rebollo invited the community on Friday at 6 p.m. to Summer Fun Fest. Mayor Rebollo spoke about the inclusion of the community as a whole and accommodating those with special needs.
